validation_scope: Schema-shape cases were checked in the external draft; semantic cases are normative acceptance obligations, not native execution evidence.

v4_additional_semantic_pairs.positive: Lawfully expired native point and companion removed together; surviving created event matches retained summary and durable complete owner disposition; current index/source proof permits terminal-only checkpoint advance.
v4_additional_semantic_pairs.negative: Same missing rows without complete owner disposition, or disposition does not cover companion removal; preserve cursor and affected-record recovery fence.
v4_additional_semantic_pairs.oracle: No rp/companion reconstruction, live availability, action, event, hold release or source resurrection in either case.

v4_additional_semantic_pairs.positive: Object-key reordering, lifecycle transition and hold-list update preserve immutable-capture SHA-256; native marker and exact capture recomputation match.
v4_additional_semantic_pairs.negative: Changed source ID, array order, timestamp spelling or safe-point value changes SHA-256; absent/wrong native recipe discriminator rejects.
v4_additional_semantic_pairs.oracle: Hash validation does not replace lifecycle/hold permission checks.

v4_additional_semantic_pairs.positive: Historical stored digest remains unchanged; admitted historical hash/custody proof validates without a new companion; optional native backfill only when complete data recomputes to same existing digest.
v4_additional_semantic_pairs.negative: Unknown original hash semantics or differing recomputation cannot be repaired by overwriting record/event digest or assigning new recipe marker.
v4_additional_semantic_pairs.oracle: No genuine historical hash rewrite and no inference of native/historical mode from timestamp or missing companion.

v5_native_semantic_pairs.positive_setup: A fully eligible point and its exact required companions are present; inject a crash immediately before and immediately after the one redb summary/removal commit.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.positive_oracle: Before commit all original keys remain and no summary exists; after commit the complete summary exists and all listed keys are absent. Retry returns the same retirement identity without another semantic effect.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.negative_setup: Inject a partial key removal, summary with a remaining conflicting point, or missing required native companion.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.negative_oracle: Preserve affected-record integrity/recovery fencing; do not infer retirement, reconstruct a point, publish an action or advance its traversal checkpoint.

v5_native_semantic_pairs.positive_setup: Complete owner release, all eleven class evaluations, inclusive 7776000-second age and exact eligible selection remain unchanged through commit.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.positive_oracle: One summary/removal transaction commits the verified selection and embedded content-free owner facts.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.negative_setup: A new protecting hold, changed release inventory, owner revision or source generation appears after selection and before CAS.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.negative_oracle: Abort the complete retirement transaction; retain all canonical custody and existing checkpoint; clear no hold.

v5_native_semantic_pairs.positive_setup: Exact admitted same-store point, required creation companion and any separately admitted required deletion companion match the closed unique retired set.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.positive_oracle: Only those one-to-three canonical keys are removed with the summary in one transaction; unrelated applications/source events remain under their owners.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.negative_setup: A required key is omitted, an unregistered fourth custody family is inserted, or a target belongs to another transaction store.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.negative_oracle: Retirement remains unavailable with zero partial removal; no best-effort cross-store cleanup or invented optional companion.

v5_native_semantic_pairs.positive_setup: The mandatory backup boundary carries the canonical retained summary and the current verified source/survivor authority.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.positive_oracle: Recovery preserves the terminal summary result and cannot reactivate an older pre-retirement point.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.negative_setup: A candidate backup lacks required summary custody or an unexplained missing point is paired only with a lifecycle event.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.negative_oracle: Disclose incomplete recovery and preserve affected-point fencing; do not choose the incomplete candidate as complete authority or fabricate a summary.

v5_native_semantic_pairs.positive_setup: Advance one validated projection generation through 100 source records with repeated full current-source/index proof.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.positive_oracle: Publication identity, generation birth and prior history stay fixed; the cursor advances atomically without consuming another generation slot.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.negative_setup: Each cursor update mints a new generation, archives the old cursor, slides a birth/retirement time or skips current source proof.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.negative_oracle: Reject the invalid checkpoint publication and preserve prior durable coverage; no per-event retention-slot exhaustion is introduced.

v5_native_semantic_pairs.positive_setup: A verified rebuild publishes a distinct generation with a lawful slot and preserves final predecessor cursor and existing older retirement facts.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.positive_oracle: One transaction archives the exact prior core with retirement time equal to the new birth and successor equal to the new generation ID.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.negative_setup: Transition supplies stale predecessor bytes, self-successor, inconsistent time, protected-history eviction or an archived cursor as current coverage.
v5_native_semantic_pairs.negative_oracle: Reject publication without changing prior authority, retirement anchors or holds; disclose unavailable currentness where no lawful slot exists.
